_schema: The video antenna — the third component LTHL-11 unbundled out of Build.ELECTRONICS_MASS_G's 35 g remainder. Two tiers, as everywhere else: `specs` is physics-bearing and `catalog` is browsing metadata only. Colour, price and vendor links are banned by name, from either block. WHAT THE PHYSICS READS IS THE THREE DIMENSIONS AND THE MASS. Gain and polarisation are in `catalog`: Lothal has no radio model and nothing computes a link budget, so a gain figure in `specs` would be a claim that the sim reads it. THE ANTENNA IS THE MOST OFTEN FORGOTTEN MASS ON A BUILD AND THE ONE FURTHEST FROM THE CENTRE. An SMA whip on a rear mast is 8 g sitting a plate-length behind the centre of mass, and it is the largest single fore/aft moment among the four components this slice unbundled — which is precisely why giving it a real mount was worth doing rather than leaving it in a lump at the origin. MASS COMES OUT OF THE BUDGET, NEVER ADDED BESIDE IT — Build.ANTENNA_BUDGET_MASS_G (5 g). The default entry weighs exactly that, so the reference build is unmoved at 496.0 g. OMITTING IT COSTS ZERO GRAMS, and a build with a VTX and no antenna is a real (if unwise) build rather than an impossible one; Lothal warns and never blocks, and this file does not even warn — it simply weighs what is fitted. 'mounting' says TRAY: an antenna is held by a bracket, a mast or a zip tie, at no spacing any frame publishes. Entries are ordered by mass. THE MASSES HERE ARE CLASS-TYPICAL RATHER THAN RE-SOURCED FROM ONE TEST REGIME, and each entry's `source` says so. OPTIONAL specs.mount_diameter_mm (printed-room PR3b): the diameter of the barrel or coax a printed antenna mount's tube holds. When present the Printed room bores to it; when absent it falls back to width_mm and says so. No entry publishes it yet, and none is to be invented.

parts.name: Nano dipole (u.FL)
parts.source: representative u.FL linear dipole of the class fitted to whoops and toothpicks — a length of coax and a whip, with no connector body. Class-typical, not a specific product. NOT re-sourced from one test regime — see _schema.

parts.name: DJI O4 Air Unit Pro antennas (pair)
parts.source: DJI 'O4 Air Unit Series' specifications page (dji.com/o4-air-unit/specs), O4 Air Unit Pro column: 'Antenna: Approx. 2.1 g/pcs' and 'Antenna: 110 mm'. THIS ENTRY IS THE PAIR, AND THAT IS A DEPARTURE FROM THE REST OF THIS FILE, which weighs one antenna per entry. The O4 Air Unit Pro is a dual-antenna system — DJI's own 15 km transmission figure is quoted for the pair — so an aircraft carrying it carries two, and 2 x 2.1 = 4.2 g. The alternative was two fitted antennas, which the mass model has no category for, or one, which would under-weigh every O4 aircraft by 2.1 g. The cost is that the inertia box is one 110 mm stick where the aircraft has two, which is the smaller error of the two available and is written down here rather than left to be discovered. Gain is 'not published' rather than a number, since DJI states none and this file's _schema keeps unread claims out of `catalog` as firmly as out of `specs`.

parts.name: RHCP u.FL (5.8 GHz)
parts.source: representative circularly-polarised u.FL antenna on a short pigtail — the 5" freestyle class's default, and the reference build's. Its mass is exactly Build.ANTENNA_BUDGET_MASS_G so the reference build is unmoved. NOT re-sourced from one test regime — see _schema.

parts.name: RHCP SMA (5.8 GHz)
parts.source: representative circularly-polarised antenna with an SMA connector body and a rear mast mount; the connector and the mast are most of the difference in mass from the u.FL entry. Class-typical, not a specific product. NOT re-sourced from one test regime — see _schema.

parts.name: RHCP SMA long-range (5.8 GHz)
parts.source: representative higher-gain circularly-polarised airborne antenna of the class flown on long-range builds; class-typical, not a specific product. NOT re-sourced from one test regime — see _schema.
